Lessons.Title: Areas under a Normal Curve
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Determine areas under a normal curve. Interpret (orally and in writing) the proportion of values in certain intervals under a normal curve in a variety of different contexts.

The standard normal probability between z=-1 and z=1 is approximately0.6827, and the complement outside that interval about0.3173. These are model-based proportions, not exact counts for arbitrary finite samples.

The area under the curve to the left of 39 is 0.3085. The area under the curve to the left of 43 is 0.9332. The area under the curve to the left of 43 is 0.9332. Since it is a normal curve, we know that the total area under the curve is 1. Source activity 7.2: Life of Lights: The life span of light bulbs is approximately normally distributed. Some statistics about life spans of two different types of light bulbs are listed. LED bulbs: mean = 2,300 days, standard deviation = 230 days incandescent bulbs: mean = 100 days, standard deviation = 10 days To estimate the proportion of bulbs that burn out in a certain interval of time, use technology to… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 7.3: Waiting for a Waiter: The wait times at a popular restaurant are approximately normally distributed. The mean wait time is 24.3 minutes with a standard deviation of 3.2 minutes. Use technology to estimate the wait times for the described groups of diners. Describe the number of minutes diners have to wait if their wait times are in the longest 10% of wait times for diners at this restaurant.… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: When Lin drives a golf ball, it travels a mean distance of 200 yards with a standard deviation of 20 yards, and the distribution of lengths is approximately normal. Approximately what percentage of her shots will travel less than 180 yards? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: A distribution is approximately normal with a mean of 18 and a standard deviation of 4. Match the interval with the approximate percentage of data that falls within that interval. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Tyler looks at this histogram of a distribution with a mean of 6.7 grams and a standard deviation of 1 gram. He claims that approximately 68% of the data is between 5.7 and 7.7 grams. What is the error in his thinking? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Select all designs which describe an experimental study. 100 randomly selected students are asked if they have their driver's license. 50 baseball players are selected to wear compression sleeves during practice and games and another 50 players are selected not to wear compression sleeves during practice and games.… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: A normal curve with a mean of 400 and a standard deviation of 50 is shown. Shade the region under the curve within two standard deviations of the mean. How much of the data falls within the shaded region? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: How many data points are presented in the histogram? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
